The extra information prepared for my callback comes out incomplete: the chat and the person who sent the update are put in place correctly, but the forum topic identifier is missing from it entirely, even though what was worked out plainly carries one, so anything of mine that reads the topic id sees nothing. Items saved with descriptive text attached come back without that text, or carrying text that does not match what was entered.

This is the library an application leans on to hand messages to a broker and to read them back again, and it is getting both halves of that wrong now in a lot of small ways. The repository has received 27 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I have been able to observe from the outside, written up by what I was doing rather than by where I guess the problem lives.

Setting up a publishing client and getting messages out goes wrong early. Asking for duplicate suppression while giving the acknowledgement level as the spelled-out word is refused as a contradictory setup, even though that word names exactly the level duplicate suppression requires; the refusal goes away only if I spell the level out as a number instead. name: sdrift-sqlglot-sqlglot-003-shared
instruction_first_1500_chars:
# Align sqlglot with its documented contract

The repository at `/app` is `sqlglot` — a dependency-free SQL parser, transpiler, optimizer, and expression toolkit. Its intended behaviour is defined by its own
documentation: source docstrings, README.md, posts/ast_primer.md, and posts/onboarding.md. Right now the implementation and the documentation disagree; the code runs,
but at certain inputs it returns something the documentation says it should not.

Your task: study the documented behaviour, compare it to the code, and change the implementation so it
matches the documentation wherever the two disagree. Preserve public callable names, parameter names
and order, and file layout; restore defaults when the documentation specifies them.
Edit only files under `/app/sqlglot/`, and add no new files. There is no network
access. Correctness is measured against documented public behavior throughout the library,
so align to the documentation itself rather than to any particular test.

Before editing, write a short plan to /app/NOTES.md — what the docs specify, where the code diverges, and how you'll verify your fix — then implement it.

# aiogram: repairing eighteen silent behaviour regressions without a test suite

A program of mine that talks to a chat service through this library has started misbehaving in a great many small ways at once, and what follows is everything I noticed after moving it onto this checkout. Nothing about the service changed and nothing in my own program changed; the same incoming updates that used to be dealt with correctly now come out wrong, and in several places something that used to work now raises an error instead. The repository has received 18 separate undocumented edits. The failures are spread all over, and several of them sit right next to work that still behaves perfectly.

An update coming in and being routed to whatever of mine should see it goes wrong three ways. The extra information prepared for my callback comes out incomplete: the chat and the person who sent the update are put in place correctly, but the forum topic identifier is missing from it entirely, even though what was worked out plainly carries one, so anything of mine that reads the topic id sees nothing. A condition I wrote as a lazy expression over the incoming values never evaluates at all — an inspection function I embedded in it is never called, and instead of a mapping holding the value under the name I chose, I receive the unevaluated expression itself. name: napalm-820a06b2-blind20-v2
instruction_first_1500_chars:
# napalm: diagnosing broken drivers and helpers without a test suite

Everyday work through this library — pointing it at a piece of network equipment, asking that equipment what state it is in, and pushing settings at it — now comes back with wrong answers or fails outright. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits. The equipment did not change and neither did the programs asking it things, many kinds of gear are affected, and in a couple of places one question I ask is wrong in two independent ways at once.

Even with no equipment involved, turning text a device printed into something a program can use is wrong. Handing over a human-readable running-time phrase and asking for the equivalent plain number gives totals that do not match the input, for every style of phrase: the comma-separated words ("24 days, 11 hours, 25 minutes", "1 year, 2 weeks, 5 minutes"), the days-plus-clock shorthand ("114 days, 22:27:32") and the compact letter run ("7w6d5h4m3s"). Handing over a small block of aligned text — a heading, a line of dashes, a line of data — along with its column widths no longer yields one group of column texts per line, but a far longer run of nearly empty groups, as though the input had been chewed through a character at a time.

name: dragonfly-0a80e1f5-blind20
instruction_first_1500_chars:
# Dragonfly: twenty injected faults, no test suite to find them with

This library drives a sandbox mining-and-building game, and a great deal of what a player does in it now comes out wrong. Nothing about the rules of the game changed and nothing about my own code changed, yet the same actions that used to give the right result now give a different one, and in several places something that used to happen does not happen at all. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I have been able to observe from the outside.

Digging with a tool in hand is mistimed everywhere I look. Plain stone with a diamond pickaxe, the same stone while hovering off the ground, the same stone underwater both with and without the charm that cancels the water penalty, an ore struck with a wooden pickaxe too weak to harvest it at all, and the hurried and the sluggish potion cases alike: every single one of them reports a time that disagrees with the figure I worked out by hand, all skewed the same way. Separately, a diamond pickaxe bearing a level-three digging-speed charm now digs at exactly the pace of a bare one, so the soft red rock of the lower realm it used to clear instantly now takes measurable effort, as though that charm did not belong on a digging tool at all.

We put Trickster (influxdb backend, in-memory cache) in front of our InfluxDB 1.8 server. Since then, open the CPU panel on prod, flip to stage, and stage draws prod's line, or the other way round. Widen the time range after a flip and the older half of the graph comes from one environment, the newer half from the other. The same queries sent straight to InfluxDB are right for both. Restarting Trickster clears it until the next flip.

instruction_first_1500_chars:

overwrite someone else's change. Since we moved the customer store to Postgres jsonb, every
address edit is rejected with a failed test, even when nobody touched the record in between.
Edits to plain fields like the name still go through.
